# Low-risk and informational alerts are reported but do not block the medium/high gate; only rows below are suppressed.
# This file is read by scripts/check-zap-severity.mjs, NOT by ZAP itself: it is a
# 7-column reviewed-exception ledger, not ZAP's 2-column rule config, so the
# workflow deliberately does not pass it via `rules_file_name`.
# The row below corresponds to a real finding from the first recorded run against
# the demo runtime (see GSA/sam-layouts#80 for the raw counts). It is not header
# noise and is not dismissed: it is scoped as narrowly as the finding allows,
# points at a tracking issue, and carries an expiry that forces a re-review.

column7: The demo shell renders app-nx-welcome, a generated scaffolding component with encapsulation: ViewEncapsulation.None and a literal <style> block in its template, so the served CSP must allow style-src 'unsafe-inline' or the page the scanner crawls does not render. Tightening the header purely to clear this alert would make the scanned headers unrepresentative of what the demo actually needs, which is worse than a documented waiver. Every other CSP directive is locked down and the published 'layouts' library is unaffected — the demo app is internal tooling with no runtime surface in the package. GSA/ngx-uswds baselines the same rule for the same reason. Scope is the DAST server's own origin, so the waiver can never follow this policy into a real deployment. Prefer a nonce or hash over renewing this if the demo shell is reworked.
